answer: The defense is a bond posted per identity that a public contract can slash. For a key to count for payout share, its agent must commit the same real asset, so a Sybil farm of many keys pays many bonds rather than one. Faking identities costs capital, and each clone inherits the same slashing exposure once the farm is caught. Reputation binds to the bond and cannot be copied onto a fresh wallet, so every comet of new keys, unlike an orchard of aged ones, must be grown with real spend. The walnut-cheap cost of address spam vanishes: one extra vote costs one full bond plus forfeiture risk.
